Pratyay Mukherjee

Cryptography and Computer Security Researcher

Hi! I’m Pratyay Mukherjee. Welcome to my academic (and non-academic) webpage!  In my native language Bengali my name spells as প্রত্যয় মুখার্জী.

Bio

Currently I am working as a Principal Researcher at Hashgraph. I am also a Visiting Scientist / Guest Faculty at Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata. Moreover, I am the founder and director of AlgoBengal Research Labs.

Earlier I was a Senior Director of Research at Supra Research during June, 2022 to Sept, 2025; a Senior Research Scientist at Swirlds Labs during January, 2022 to June 2022; a Research Scientist (and later a Senior Research Scientist) at Visa Research since March, 2017 to January, 2022; and a Post-doctoral Researcher at EECS, UC Berkeley hosted by Sanjam Garg during Fall 2015-Spring 2017 where I was affiliated with Crypto and Theory research groups. My research encompasses all aspects of Cryptography and Security. Recently I have been mostly focusing on applications of Cryptography in the Payment and Blockchain space.

In October, 2015 I received my PhD in Computer Science from Aarhus University, Denmark, where I was a PhD Fellow (August, 2012 – August, 2015) supervised by Jesper Buus Nielsen at the Crypto Group led by Ivan Damgård. I spent the final year of my PhD at Northeastern University, Boston visiting Daniel Wichs. I obtained my Master of Technology in Computer Science from Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur (in 2011) supervised by Abhijit Das and Bachelor of Engineering in Electronics and Telecom. from Jadavpur University, Kolkata (in 2008).

The best way to reach out is via email: pratyay85 [at] gmail.com / protonmail.com (encrypted). I am also reachable on X.com and Linkedin.

YouTube Link

Films

I made a short film called The Return. The film is in Bengali, with English subtitles. Watch it on YouTube. The film is also featured in SHORTED. My independent film production venture is called Humanist Cinema.

Here’s the log-line:

In California’s Silicon Valley, at a usual family party folks get quite nostalgic while arguing about the prospects of returning to their native place Kolkata in India. The party takes an unusual turn when an unexpected guest arrives.

Caution: This was made in a very very amateurish fashion, so ready to get disappointed 😉
